text:
chen: heads-up — perf-ci on main flagged the longctx suite: ~-26% throughput and intermittent OOMs in kv-cache tests.
deploy-bot: perf-ci/job-longctx (commit abcdef1) failed: 3/10 runs OOM, mean tokens/s down 26%.
alex: repro'd locally on a dev box with --seqlen 8192, OOM after ~2 minutes. command I used: `./scripts/run_perf --model=opt-13b --seqlen=8192 --batch=1`
priya: any recent merges touching KV eviction heuristics or kernel routing?
chen: yes — PR #4872 merged yesterday. it changed eviction to a windowed-LRU (window_size=64) AND tweaked kernel routing priorities for long-sequence transformers.
jason: assigning a bisect to @alex and @priya to confirm.
alex: quick bisect completed — regression introduced by commit abcdef1 (PR #4872). reverting that commit locally restores throughput and prevents the OOMs.
maria: dropping a short profile snapshot from the failing run:
```
kv_slab_usage: 94% (growing)
largest_free_block: 128KB -> fragmentation spike
alloc_stack: runtime/kernel_router.cpp:142 -> kv_cache.cc:312
OOM at kv_cache.cc:487 (alloc of 2.1MB failed)
repro cmd: ./bin/serve --mode=bench --seq 8192 --trace kv
```
priya: hypothesis: windowed-LRU keeps many small hot windows alive, increasing fragmentation on slabs. combined with the kernel routing change we now route long-seq work to a path that delays compaction/swap triggers. result: steady slab growth until OOM.
chen: exact — I see the kernel path skips the aggressive compaction for `seq >= 4096` to reduce latency, but that assumption relied on a less-fragmenting eviction policy.
jason: short-term mitigation: set KV_EVICT_WINDOW=16 and revert kernel-selector to `legacy_large_seq` for routes with seq>4096. anyone object?
alex: doing a smoke run with those env overrides now.
alex: smoke looks good locally — no OOM after 10 runs, tokens/s back to baseline.
chen: I'll open a hotfix PR that reverts the kernel-routing change and narrows the window-lru defaults. PR #4890. includes a unit test that simulates heavy small-window churn.
maria: CI for #4890 shows perf recovered on the longctx job but deploy blocked: "can't hotpatch runtime until maintenance window" :zzz: — ops flagged scheduled maintenance for tonight.
priya: can we route prod longctx traffic to a safe fallback while we wait for the window? @infra-bot can you assist?
infra-bot: routing change applied: longctx-* -> dedicated-fallback-us-west. confirms routes, monitoring started.
jason: good. also adding a perf-regression alert for kernel-selector and KV_EVICT_* changes so next merge will trip an early guard.
chen: follow-ups: 1) revert landed in staging + rollout plan, 2) add an integration test that ramps many small prefixes to exercise fragmentation, 3) add perf alert on slab growth >70% over 5m.
alex: adding the repro script and the `--kv-trace` flag to longctx CI so we capture alloc traces for future regressions.
maria: we'll assemble a short postmortem with timeline and root cause once hotfix is deployed. :memo:
priya: thanks everyone — tagging eng-runtime to pick this up for full revert + tests.
chen: ack. great collaboration, saved the rollout. :thumbsup:
